rows.consequence: An operator following the stale packs could add observations after seeing the outcome while retaining confirmatory language, invalidating nominal confirmatory coverage. Repeating the normative rule in each pack multiplies the repair and future-drift surface.
rows.counterevidence: The affected packs are pre-hardware drafts; registry freeze and the downstream claims linter provide later control points. The split-suite pack correctly freezes n and names exploratory demotion, so the canonical behavior is available as a migration pattern.
evidence_refs: Bounded absence/contrast search: git grep -n -E 'top up|top-up|Top up|Top-up' BASE_HEAD -- docs/campaign_packs returned the stale rows above and the three D-062-compliant split-suite rows.
rows.finding: Eight campaign-pack files duplicate the MDE/sample-size rule and direct outcome-dependent top-ups when an observed confidence interval touches the floor or leave-one-out changes the verdict, without the permanent exploratory demotion required by canonical D-062. The split-suite pack has already been updated to the canonical frozen-n rule, demonstrating policy drift among copied rows.

campaign sizing instructions ↔ confirmatory claim eligibility

rows.consequence: Manifest readers can reasonably infer that values such as cold_between_bundles or bundle_only are enforced when they are not enforced through these fields. The constants also add generator, schema, manifest, and test surface without enabling a behavior choice.
rows.counterevidence: Other execution-policy fields are real: adapters consume order_policy and default_output_policy. Cooldown/cache behavior may be enforced independently by controller/config/process lifecycle, and retaining descriptive declarations inside hashed manifests can aid provenance.
evidence_refs: Bounded absence search: for each of cooldown_policy, cache_policy, warmup_policy, within_bundle_repeats, status_policy, git grep across BASE_HEAD joulewise/ and scripts/ excluding suite.py and the two manifest generators returned no runtime consumer.
Bounded counter-search found order_policy/default_output_policy consumers at joulewise/adapters/mlx_runtime.py:276,439,455 and joulewise/adapters/mock_runtime.py:211,364,385.
rows.finding: The suite schema exposes execution_policy.cooldown_policy, cache_policy, warmup_policy, and within_bundle_repeats plus per-item status_policy as operational-looking knobs, but the pinned runtime has no consumer for them. within_bundle_repeats is only accepted when equal to 1, status_policy only accepts 'none', and 84 manifest items repeat that constant.
